touches.text: Commit often. WHY: so we never wind up with stray files or incomplete work.
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.

Deleting code is about running code, not about the record of what happened. A retired path that something still CALLS is the defect; a retired path named by a record of what passed through (history, state, validations, verdicts, a measured fixture) is not. Requirements that police history are de-emphasized, because the aim is less history noise in front of Claude, not hidden history (Law 5). Akien 2026-11-13, answering Q#99 (ticket c8e421aac06e's measured fixture names skills/ruled/intention+why.json and the retirement tooth read it as a caller): "we are trying to remove as much of the history as we can. not hiding it, but reducing the noise you're exposed to. time to de-emphasize requirements like that."
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.

A tooth whose live subject was deleted retires with it, when fixture teeth still cover the behaviour. Akien 2026-11-12, answering Q#87 (ce92eb562cf9 clause 6 read 6890cf7e4053's clause-2 tooth, deleted with the inference_calls table by 98ab0e9db57f): "i am good with retiring that".

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal. Akien 2026-11-13, answering Q#90 (a Windows reseal of a mixed proof overwrote the Linux seal, measured 2026-11-12): "then we have to invent a way for seals to be host independent. one way would be to create a sealing machine in cairn. there's only ever one cairn until we have a laptop die and have to fail over to a backup".
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
